mainTopic: Which מנחות need oil and frankincense, and the ברייתא's word-by-word sources from the פסוק of the עומר
overview: This amud opens a משנה that sorts the מנחות (meal offerings) into four groups based on two ingredients, oil (שמן) and frankincense (לבונה). Most מנחות need both. The מנחת נסכים needs only oil, the לחם הפנים needs only frankincense, and the שתי הלחם, the מנחת חוטא and the מנחת קנאות need neither. The גמרא begins with רב פפא's rule that wherever the משנה says 'ten,' all ten loaves must be of one kind, against רבי שמעון. A ברייתא then reads the פסוק about the עומר word by word. 'עליה' keeps oil off the לחם הפנים and frankincense off the מנחת נסכים, even though a קל וחומר would have suggested otherwise. 'מנחה' adds the מנחת שמיני to frankincense, and 'היא' leaves out the שתי הלחם. The גמרא then asks why each word points to that offering and not to the מנחת כהנים. It answers by comparing features with the עומר, and when the comparison is a tie, the word 'נפש' decides. The amud ends with an אדרבה challenge about the שתי הלחם that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Four groups of meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens by saying there are four kinds of מנחות, based on whether they need oil, frankincense, both, or neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are meal offerings that need oil and frankincense, some that need oil but not frankincense, some that need frankincense but not oil, and some that need neither frankincense nor oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a general outline of four groups of מנחות. It is setting up the lists that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ingredients, שמן and לבונה, and each can be present or missing, which gives four combinations. Every מנחה fits into one of these four boxes. The rest of the משנה fills in each box with examples.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: the opening teaching that the גמרא will discuss
They require. This means these ingredients must be included
Oil (olive oil) mixed into or poured on the offering
Frankincense, a fragrant spice placed on the offering

steps.whatToRemember: Two ingredients (שמן and לבונה) give four possible groups of מנחות.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There are those that require oil and frankincense,
phrases.notes: The word מנחות is left out but assumed: every case here is a kind of meal offering.

phrases.english: oil but not frankincense,
frankincense but not oil,
neither frankincense nor oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנחות divide into four groups depending on whether they require שמן, לבונה, both, or neither.

steps.title: Offerings that need both oil and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the מנחות that need both שמן and לבונה: the five voluntary types, plus the מנחות of כהנים, the כהן משיח, a גוי, women, and the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: These need oil and frankincense: the fine-flour offering, the pan offering, the deep-pan offering, the oven-baked loaves and wafers, the priests' offering, the anointed priest's offering, a gentile's offering, women's offerings, and the עומר offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה fills in the first group: the offerings that need both oil and frankincense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line lists the regular kinds of מנחה a person can choose to bring, which differ in how they are cooked. The second line adds offerings that are special because of who brings them (כהנים, the כהן משיח, a גוי, women) or because of the occasion (the עומר). All of them still need both ingredients.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine-flour meal offering, brought as uncooked flour
A flat pan: an offering fried on a griddle
A deep pan: an offering cooked in a deep pot
Loaves and wafers: the two forms of an oven-baked מנחה
The anointed priest, meaning the כהן גדול
The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the five items in the first line are five unrelated offerings. חלות and רקיקין are two forms of the same oven-baked מנחה.

phrases.english: And these require oil and frankincense:
the fine-flour meal offering, and the pan offering,
and the deep-pan offering,
and the loaves, and the wafers.
The meal offering of priests, the meal offering of the anointed priest,
the meal offering of a gentile, the meal offering of women,
the omer meal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first of the four groups introduced in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five voluntary מנחות and the מנחות of כהנים, the כהן משיח, a גוי, women, and the עומר all require both שמן and לבונה.

steps.title: The libation offering needs oil only
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת נסכים needs שמן but not לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The meal offering brought with libations requires oil, but does not require frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה fills in the second group with an offering that needs only oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת נסכים is not a stand-alone offering. It comes along with an animal offering, together with the wine libation. This משנה tells us that it gets oil but no frankincense.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering that accompanies an animal sacrifice along with its wine libation
Libations, the wine poured as part of a sacrifice
And it does not require

phrases.english: The meal offering of libations requires oil,
but does not require frankincense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first group to the second group (oil but not frankincense)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנחת נסכים requires שמן and does not require לבונה.

steps.title: The shewbread needs frankincense only
steps.stepSummary: The לחם הפנים needs לבונה but not שמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The shewbread requires frankincense, but does not require oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה fills in the third group with an offering that is the reverse of the previous one: frankincense but no oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Set next to the מנחת נסכים, the לחם הפנים shows the opposite pattern. It has לבונה but no שמן. With this, three of the four groups have examples, and the group that needs neither ingredient is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: The shewbread: twelve loaves placed on the שולחן in the משכן or מקדש
Requires (the masculine form, because לחם is masculine)

steps.whatToRemember: So far: most מנחות need both; מנחת נסכים needs only oil; לחם הפנים needs only frankincense.

phrases.english: The shewbread requires frankincense,
but does not require oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third group (frankincense but not oil), the reverse of step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לחם הפנים requires לבונה and does not require שמן.

steps.title: Three מנחות that need neither oil nor frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes its list: the שתי הלחם, the מנחת חוטא, and the מנחת קנאות need neither שמן nor לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two loaves of שבועות, the meal offering of a sinner, and the meal offering of jealousy need neither oil nor frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its four-way list by naming the fourth group: מנחות that get neither oil nor frankincense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the four categories from Step 1. The first group needed both, the second only oil, the third only frankincense, and now the last group needs neither. The מנחת חוטא and the מנחת קנאות are offerings tied to sin or suspicion, and the תורה explicitly says not to add oil or frankincense to them.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The poor sinner's flour offering, brought instead of an animal or birds
The 'jealousy' offering brought by a סוטה, a woman suspected by her husband

steps.whatToRemember: The four groups are: both (most מנחות), oil only (מנחת נסכים), frankincense only (לחם הפנים), and neither (שתי הלחם, מנחת חוטא, מנחת קנאות).

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם, וּמִנְחַת חוֹטֵא, וּמִנְחַת קְנָאוֹת
phrases.english: The two loaves, and the meal offering of a sinner, and the meal offering of jealousy
phrases.notes: The 'meal offering of jealousy' is the one brought by a סוטה (במדבר 5:15).

phrases.aramaic: – אֵין טְעוּנִין לֹא שֶׁמֶן וְלֹא לְבוֹנָה.
phrases.english: do not require oil and do not require frankincense.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין טְעוּנִין לֹא שֶׁמֶן וְלֹא לְבוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the four-category list begun in Step 1 by naming the final group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שתי הלחם, the מנחת חוטא, and the מנחת קנאות get neither oil nor frankincense.

steps.title: רב פפא: ten loaves must all be of one kind
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא teaches that whenever the משנה says to bring ten, all ten must be of the same type. This rejects רבי שמעון, who allows half חלות and half רקיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Wherever we learned 'ten' in a משנה, we learned ten of one kind. This rules out רבי שמעון, who says one may bring half loaves and half wafers. רב פפא teaches us that one may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a general rule from רב פפא about how to read the number 'ten' in the משניות of מנחות, and then explains which opinion this rule rejects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some baked מנחות are brought as ten pieces, either thick loaves (חלות) or thin wafers (רקיקין). רבי שמעון allowed mixing them, five and five. רב פפא says the plain משנה means ten of a single type, so mixing is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to rule out a different opinion
Thick loaves
Thin wafers
He is teaching us (a new point)

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying every מנחה has ten pieces. He is saying that wherever the משנה does say 'ten,' the ten cannot be a mix of loaves and wafers.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Pappa said:
Anywhere that we learned 'ten', we learned [ten of one kind],
phrases.notes: Literally 'we learned ten, we learned ten.' He means the משנה really meant ten whole items of one kind.

phrases.english: to exclude the view of Rabbi Shimon, who says:
He may bring half loaves and half wafers,
he teaches us that he may not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דִּתְנַן עֶשֶׂר – תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא with a general reading rule for the משניות of the מסכת, not tied directly to the list in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the משנה says ten, all ten must be of one type, against רבי שמעון's permission to bring half and half.

steps.title: Source: oil goes on the מנחה, not on the לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'ונתת עליה שמן' that oil is put on 'it,' the מנחה, and not on the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And you shall put oil upon it.' Oil goes on it, but not on the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the פסוק behind the משנה's rule that the לחם הפנים gets no oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the עומר says to put oil 'upon it.' The ברייתא reads the word 'it' as limiting: only this kind of מנחה gets oil. That limit leaves out the לחם הפנים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall put oil upon it' (ויקרא 2:15)
'Upon it,' the word that limits the oil to this מנחה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And you shall put oil upon it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:15, said about the עומר מנחה.

phrases.english: but not oil upon the shewbread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's list and gives the source for Step 4's rule that the לחם הפנים has no oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'עליה' limits oil to the מנחה and excludes the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: Why a פסוק is needed: a קל וחומר would add oil
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains why the limiting word was needed. A קל וחומר could have argued that the לחם הפנים needs oil: if the מנחת נסכים has no frankincense yet gets oil, then the לחם הפנים, which does get frankincense, should surely get oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might have thought: Is it not logical? If the מנחת נסכים, which does not need frankincense, does need oil, then the לחם הפנים, which does need frankincense, should surely need oil!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises the logical argument that the פסוק has to block. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר treats frankincense as a sign of importance. The מנחת נסכים lacks that importance and still gets oil, so the more important לחם הפנים should get oil too. This explains why the word 'עליה' is not extra: without it, we would have reached the wrong conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: For one might have thought
Is it not logical? (opening of a קל וחומר)
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final law. It is the 'you might have thought' argument that the פסוק comes to block.

phrases.english: For one might have thought: Is it not logical?
Now, if the meal offering of libations,
which does not require frankincense, requires oil,
then the shewbread, which does require frankincense,
is it not logical that it requires oil?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the limiting word in Step 7 is needed by showing the logical argument it overrides.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word 'עליה' to exclude the לחם הפנים from oil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the מנחת נסכים (oil without frankincense) would require oil for the לחם הפנים (which has frankincense).

steps.title: The word 'עליה' overrides the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the word 'עליה' blocks the קל וחומר: oil goes on the מנחה, not on the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the פסוק says 'upon it': oil upon it, but not oil upon the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the קל וחומר by pointing back to the word 'עליה,' which shuts down the logical argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clear word in the פסוק outweighs a logical argument. Because the קל וחומר would have added oil to the לחם הפנים, the תורה needed to write 'עליה' to exclude it. The rule from Step 4 now stands with a firm source.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says (introducing the verse that settles the issue)

steps.whatToRemember: The לחם הפנים gets no oil because the פסוק says 'עליה,' even though a קל וחומר from the מנחת נסכים would have suggested otherwise.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common pattern: the גמרא proves a word in the פסוק is needed by showing what we would wrongly conclude without it.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states "upon it":
oil upon it,
but not oil upon the shewbread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of Step 8 by relying on the limiting word quoted in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides a logical derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By קל וחומר from the מנחת נסכים, the לחם הפנים should need oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'עליה' limits oil to the מנחה, so the לחם הפנים gets no oil.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The לחם הפנים is excluded from oil by the word 'עליה.'

steps.title: No frankincense on the libations offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads 'ושמת עליה לבונה' to teach that frankincense goes on 'it,' and not on the מנחת נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you shall put frankincense on it': frankincense goes on it, but not on the מנחה that comes with wine libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from oil to frankincense. It uses the same word 'עליה' to leave out the מנחת נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the oil teaching in Step 7. There 'עליה' kept oil off the לחם הפנים, and here it keeps frankincense off the מנחת נסכים. The next steps explain why this limiting word was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, placed on many מנחות
The flour offering brought along with the wine libations of an animal sacrifice
'On it', a limiting word: on this offering only

phrases.english: "And you shall put frankincense on it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:15

phrases.english: Frankincense goes on it,
but not frankincense on the meal-offering of libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels the oil derivation of Steps 7–9, now applied to frankincense.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת נסכים does not get לבונה.

steps.title: A קל וחומר that would require frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows why the limiting word was needed. Since the לחם הפנים gets frankincense without oil, the מנחת נסכים, which does get oil, should surely get frankincense.
steps.simpleTranslation: For you might have thought: isn't it logical? If the showbread, which does not need oil, does need frankincense, then the libations offering, which does need oil, should surely need frankincense!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא builds a logical argument that would have given the מנחת נסכים frankincense. It is setting up why 'עליה' had to be written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the קל וחומר in Step 8. There the לחם הפנים seemed to deserve oil. Here the מנחת נסכים seems to deserve frankincense, because it already gets the oil that the לחם הפנים lacks.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it logical?', the opening of a קל וחומר
Requires, needs
The showbread placed on the שולחן in the Temple

phrases.english: For one might have said: isn't it logical?

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים שֶׁאֵינוֹ טָעוּן שֶׁמֶן –
phrases.english: If the showbread, which does not need oil,
does need frankincense,
then the libations meal-offering, which does need oil,
isn't it logical that it needs frankincense?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the exclusion in Step 10 was necessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the limiting word 'עליה' regarding frankincense
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the לחם הפנים (no oil, yet frankincense) suggests the מנחת נסכים (with oil) must get frankincense.

steps.title: The word 'on it' blocks the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'עליה' to override the logic: frankincense goes on the מנחת העומר and not on the מנחת נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the verse says 'on it': frankincense goes on it, and not on the libations offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own setup. The word 'עליה' cancels the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clear word in the פסוק beats a logical argument. That is why the תורה needed to write 'עליה': without it we would have used the קל וחומר and added frankincense.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches', introducing the word that settles the question

steps.whatToRemember: The מנחת נסכים gets oil but no frankincense, and the לחם הפנים gets frankincense but no oil. Each is excluded by 'עליה'.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says "on it":
frankincense on it,
and not frankincense on the libations meal-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קל וחומר of Step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By קל וחומר, the מנחת נסכים would need frankincense.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עליה' limits frankincense to the מנחת העומר, so the מנחת נסכים gets none.

steps.title: Including the eighth-day offering, excluding the two loaves
steps.stepSummary: The word 'מנחה' adds the מנחת שמיני to the frankincense requirement. The word 'היא' excludes the שתי הלחם from both oil and frankincense.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A meal-offering' includes the meal-offering of the eighth day for frankincense. 'It is' excludes the two loaves, so they need neither oil nor frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads two more words from the same פסוק. One word adds an offering and the other leaves one out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מנחה' is read as including another offering: the מנחת שמיני, which the תורה describes without frankincense, also gets it. 'היא' is read as narrowing: the שתי הלחם of שבועות get neither oil nor frankincense. This is the source for the משנה's ruling in Step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, to add a case
To exclude, to leave a case out
The מנחה brought on the eighth day of the inauguration of the משכן
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

phrases.english: "A meal-offering" includes the meal-offering of the eighth day for frankincense,
phrases.notes: These words come from 'מנחה היא' in ויקרא 2:15. The eighth-day offering is in ויקרא 9:4.

phrases.english: "It is" excludes the two loaves,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יִטְעֲנוּ לֹא שֶׁמֶן וְלֹא לְבוֹנָה.
phrases.english: so that they need neither oil nor frankincense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's word-by-word reading of the same פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the scriptural source for the משנה's ruling that the שתי הלחם need neither oil nor frankincense.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת שמיני needs לבונה, and the שתי הלחם need neither שמן nor לבונה.

steps.title: Why exclude the showbread and not the priests' offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that 'oil on it' excludes the לחם הפנים. It asks why that word should not instead exclude the מנחת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'oil on it,' and not oil on the showbread. But say instead: 'oil on it,' and not oil on the priests' meal-offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to Step 7 and challenges it. Maybe the limiting word 'עליה' is leaving out a different offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An exclusion word only shows that something is left out; it does not say what. The גמרא suggests the מנחת כהנים as an equally good candidate. If so, the לחם הפנים would no longer be excluded from oil, and the ברייתא's conclusion would be shaken.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say instead', proposing a different reading
A meal-offering brought by a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: 'אמר מר' is not a new ruling. It quotes the ברייתא from Step 7 so the גמרא can challenge it.

phrases.english: The Master said: "oil on it"
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from Step 7.

phrases.english: and not oil on the showbread.
Say instead: "oil on it"
and not oil on the priests' meal-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the oil teaching of Steps 7–9 and questions which offering it excludes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim (Step 7) that 'עליה' excludes the לחם הפנים from oil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The limiting word could just as well exclude the מנחת כהנים, so it is not clear why it was applied to the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: The priests' meal offering is more like the עומר: six similarities
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it makes sense to include the מנחת כהנים in the oil requirement. It shares six features with the מנחת העומר that the לחם הפנים does not have.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands to reason that the מנחת כהנים is the one that should be included, since it is like the עומר in six ways: a tenth of an איפה, a vessel, brought outside, the rule about its form, being brought near the altar, and the fires of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14. The מנחת כהנים is the more natural one to include with the עומר for oil, so the excluding word must be leaving out the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a פסוק includes one item and leaves out another, we include the item that looks more like the main case. The main case here is the מנחת העומר. The מנחת כהנים matches it in six ways, so it gets the oil, and the exclusion falls on the לחם הפנים.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes more sense
A tenth of an איפה, the measure of flour used
'Form': the offering becomes disqualified if it is left overnight
Bringing the מנחה near to the southwest corner of the altar
The fires of the altar; part or all of the offering is burned

steps.confusionAlert: Each word in the list is shorthand for a full rule. 'כלי' means both offerings are made holy in a service vessel. 'חוץ' means both are offered on the outer altar, while the לחם הפנים is placed on the Table inside.

phrases.aramaic: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי,
phrases.english: It stands to reason that he should include the meal offering of priests,
phrases.notes: Include it with the מנחת העומר in needing oil. The עומר is the offering the פסוק is talking about.

phrases.english: as it shares with it: a tenth, a vessel,
outside, and form, bringing near, and the fires.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14's question about why the לחם הפנים is the one left out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparing similarities: the case that is more similar to the main case is the one included
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the word should leave out the מנחת כהנים and include the לחם הפנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחת כהנים shares six features with the עומר, so it is included in the oil requirement and the לחם הפנים is left out.

steps.title: On the contrary: the showbread shares three features with the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back with אדרבה. The לחם הפנים also has things in common with the מנחת העומר: both are communal, both are obligatory, and both can be brought in impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, the לחם הפנים is the one that should be included, since it is like the עומר in being communal, obligatory, and allowed even in impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It shows that the לחם הפנים has its own strong points of similarity with the עומר, so the choice is not as obvious as it seemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 compared the offerings by how they are physically handled. This step compares them by what kind of offering they are. The עומר and the לחם הפנים are both communal and required offerings, while the מנחת כהנים is a private and voluntary one. That makes it unclear which offering is really more similar.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the reasoning points the other way
Communal; brought for the whole community
Obligatory; a required offering, not a voluntary one
Impurity; communal offerings can be brought even when people are impure

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּה, לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי,
phrases.english: On the contrary, he should include the showbread,
as it shares with it: communal, obligatory, impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15's answer by offering a list of similarities that points the other way.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 15's claim that the מנחת כהנים is clearly more similar to the מנחת העומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The לחם הפנים matches the עומר in three basic features of what kind of offering it is: communal, obligatory, and allowed in impurity. So it may be the better candidate to include.

steps.title: More ways the לחם הפנים is like the מנחת העומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the אדרבה list. Like the מנחת העומר, the לחם הפנים is eaten, can become פיגול, and is brought on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לחם הפנים is also eaten, it can become פיגול, and it is brought on שבת, just like the מנחת העומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the list it started in the last step. It adds three more things the לחם הפנים shares with the מנחת העומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together with the three points from step 16, that makes six shared features, the same number the מנחת כהנים had in step 15. The מנחת כהנים is burned entirely and is not brought on שבת, so it does not share these three. So the challenge stands: why include the מנחת כהנים in the oil rule and not the לחם הפנים?

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by the intention to eat it after its allowed time
That it is eaten (by the כהנים)
The Sabbath; communal offerings are brought even then

phrases.english: That it is eaten
phrases.notes: This continues the list from the last step. The לחם הפנים is eaten by כהנים, while the מנחת כהנים is burned completely.

phrases.english: piggul,
on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of shared features begun in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 15 that the מנחת כהנים has more in common with the מנחת העומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The לחם הפנים also has six features in common with the מנחת העומר, so similarity cannot decide which one to include.

steps.title: The word נפש decides it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word 'נפש' in the פסוק points to an individual's offering, so the מנחת כהנים is the one to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes more sense to include the מנחת כהנים, because the פסוק says 'נפש', a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the tie. Since both sides have six similarities, it uses a word in the פסוק to decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section on מנחות opens with 'ונפש כי תקריב', 'when a person brings'. That wording is about an individual's offering. The מנחת כהנים is brought by an individual, while the לחם הפנים is communal, so the oil rule covers the מנחת כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes more sense
A person, which hints at an individual's offering

steps.whatToRemember: When the similarities are equal, a word in the פסוק ('נפש') breaks the tie in favor of including the individual's מנחת כהנים.

phrases.english: It stands to reason, because of 'a person.'
phrases.notes: This is the word נפש in ויקרא 2:1, 'ונפש כי תקריב', which speaks of one person's offering, like the מנחת כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אדרבה challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses a word in the פסוק to break a tie between equal similarities
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the לחם הפנים also has six similarities, maybe it should be included instead.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'נפש' points to individual offerings, so the מנחת כהנים is included and the לחם הפנים is excluded.

steps.title: Why exclude the מנחת נסכים from frankincense and not the מנחת כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that 'frankincense on it' excludes the מנחת נסכים. It asks why the line should not exclude the מנחת כהנים instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'frankincense on it', and not on the מנחת נסכים. But say instead: 'frankincense on it', and not on the מנחת כהנים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to another line of the ברייתא, this time about frankincense. It asks the same kind of question it asked about oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עליה' limits frankincense to certain offerings and leaves one out. The ברייתא said the one left out is the מנחת נסכים. The גמרא asks why it isn't the מנחת כהנים that is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, put on certain מנחות
The flour offering that comes along with an animal קרבן and its wine
A כהן's own flour offering, burned entirely
Say instead, a way of offering a different reading

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is the ברייתא we have been learning.

phrases.english: "Frankincense upon it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:15

phrases.english: and not frankincense upon the meal offering of libations.
Say instead: "Frankincense upon it"
and not frankincense upon the meal offering of priests!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the oil question and asks the same kind of question about frankincense
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement in step 12 that 'עליה' excludes the מנחת נסכים from frankincense
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'עליה' could just as easily exclude the מנחת כהנים, so why did the ברייתא pick the מנחת נסכים?

steps.title: The מנחת כהנים is a tenth mixed with a log, like the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the מנחת כהנים should be included in frankincense. Like the מנחת העומר, it is a tenth of an איפה mixed with a לוג of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes more sense to include the מנחת כהנים, since it is a tenth, mixed with a log.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the frankincense question. It shows that the מנחת כהנים is closer to the מנחת העומר than the מנחת נסכים is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the מנחת כהנים and the מנחת העומר use exactly one עשרון of flour mixed with one לוג of oil. The amounts in the מנחת נסכים change depending on which animal it comes with. So the מנחת כהנים is included in frankincense, and the מנחת נסכים is the one left out.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, a fixed measure of flour
Mixed (with oil)
A measure of liquid, here oil
To include

phrases.english: It stands to reason that the meal offering of priests
should be included,
since it is a tenth,
mixed with a log.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the frankincense question from step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that one case is more similar to the base case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe 'עליה' leaves out the מנחת כהנים from frankincense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחת כהנים matches the עומר's fixed tenth and log, so it is included, and the מנחת נסכים is left out.

steps.title: Finishing the list: brought near the altar and brought for its own sake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds the last two ways the מנחת כהנים is like the מנחת העומר. Both are brought near the altar, and both are brought for their own sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is brought near the altar, and it is brought because of itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of reasons for including the מנחת כהנים in the need for לבונה. It adds two more points it shares with the מנחת העומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 gave two points: both are a tenth of an איפה and both have a לוג of oil. Now we get two more. Both have הגשה, being brought near the altar, and both stand alone instead of coming along with an animal offering. The מנחת נסכים has neither of these, so the count is four to zero in favor of the מנחת כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Brought near: the מנחה is carried up to the corner of the altar (הַגָּשָׁה).
Because of itself: it is its own offering and does not come along with another one.

phrases.english: It is brought near the altar,
and it comes because of itself.
phrases.notes: He means it stands on its own. The מנחת נסכים only comes along with an animal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of similarities that step 20 began.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points of similarity: the מנחת כהנים matches the מנחת העומר on more features.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the extra word 'עליה' leaves out the מנחת כהנים, and the מנחת נסכים is the one included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחת כהנים shares four features with the מנחת העומר, so it is the better one to include in the need for לבונה.

steps.title: On the contrary: the libations offering also has four points in common
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the other way. The מנחת נסכים should be included instead, because it shares four other features with the מנחת העומר: it is communal, obligatory, can be brought in impurity, and is brought on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! The מנחת נסכים is the one to include, since like the מנחת העומר it is communal, obligatory, may be brought in impurity, and is brought on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It says the מנחת נסכים has just as strong a claim, with its own list of four similarities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step counted four points for the מנחת כהנים. Now the גמרא counts four different points for the מנחת נסכים. The מנחת כהנים is an individual's gift offering, so it lacks all four. Now the count is tied at four against four, and counting alone cannot decide.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour offering that comes along with an animal offering, together with wine.
To include: to add this case into the rule.
Communal: an offering that belongs to the whole community.
Brought in impurity: a communal offering can be brought even when people are טמא.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. It is a counter-list that makes the two sides equal, so the גמרא will need a different kind of proof.

phrases.english: On the contrary,
he should have included the libations meal offering,
phrases.notes: He means it should be included in the need for לבונה, like the מנחת העומר.

phrases.english: since it is communal,
obligatory, and may be brought in impurity,
and is brought on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: The words 'and it overrides' are left out but assumed: both offerings are brought even on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מִנְחַת נְסָכִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on steps 20 and 21 with an equal list of similarities for the other offering.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the מנחת כהנים is the one to include in the need for לבונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מנחת נסכים also shares four features with the מנחת העומר, so the four points for the מנחת כהנים do not decide the question.

steps.title: The word 'נפש' decides the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the tie with the פסוק. The word 'נפש' speaks about a single person's offering, so the מנחת כהנים is the one included.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to include the מנחת כהנים, because the פסוק says 'נפש', a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It uses a word in the פסוק to break the tie between the two lists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two lists are even, so the גמרא looks at the wording of the פסוק itself. 'נפש' points to offerings brought by individuals. The מנחת כהנים is an individual's offering, but the מנחת נסכים here is communal. So the מנחת כהנים is included and the מנחת נסכים is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason: this side makes more sense.
A soul, a person (ויקרא 2:1). It shows the פסוק is talking about an individual's offering.

steps.whatToRemember: When the comparisons are even (four against four), the word 'נפש' in the פסוק decides it. The מנחת כהנים, an individual's offering, is included in the need for לבונה. The מנחת נסכים is left out.

phrases.english: It stands to reason, because of “anyone” (literally, “a soul”).
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:1. Since the פסוק speaks of one person, the individual's מנחת כהנים is the better fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אדרבה challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק: a word in the text breaks the tie between the two lists.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The four points for each side cancel out, so we cannot tell which offering to include.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'נפש' points to an individual's offering, so the מנחת כהנים is included in the need for לבונה.

steps.title: Why should 'מנחה' include the eighth-day offering and not exclude it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that the word 'מנחה' includes the מנחת שמיני in the requirement of לבונה. It then asks: maybe the word comes to exclude it instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says the word 'מנחה' comes to include the meal offering of the eighth day in the need for frankincense. But maybe it comes to exclude it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word in the ברייתא, 'מנחה', which includes the מנחת שמיני in לבונה. It challenges this by asking why the word should not exclude it instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word in a פסוק can be read as including something (לרבות) or leaving it out (להוציא). The גמרא wants to know what makes the ברייתא choose 'include' here. Earlier questions (steps 14 and 19) asked which offering a limiting word leaves out; this question asks whether the word includes or excludes at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering brought on the eighth day of the inauguration of the משכן
Frankincense placed on certain meal offerings
To include, meaning the פסוק adds this case to the rule
To exclude, meaning the פסוק takes this case out of the rule
But say instead, a word used to suggest the opposite reading

phrases.english: "Meal offering" – to include the meal offering of the eighth day in the need for frankincense,
phrases.notes: This is the next word in the same פסוק, ויקרא 2:15. 'The eighth day' is the eighth day of the inauguration of the משכן.

phrases.english: But say it comes to exclude it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the 'נפש' question, the גמרא moves on to the next word of the ברייתא and applies the same include-or-exclude challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading that 'מנחה' includes the מנחת שמיני in לבונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could just as easily be read as excluding the מנחת שמיני, and nothing yet shows which reading is correct.

steps.title: Excluding would be pointless, since a one-time offering is not learned from permanent ones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Reading the word as 'include' makes sense. Reading it as 'exclude' would be useless, because we never learn a one-time offering from offerings that are brought in all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of question is that? If you say the word comes to include, that works well. But if you say it comes to exclude, why would I need it? We do not learn a one-time offering from the offerings of all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word must be including the מנחת שמיני, because a word that excludes it would teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a one-time offering (שעה) is not learned from permanent offerings (דורות). So without a פסוק, the מנחת שמיני would not need לבונה at all, and a פסוק to exclude it would be wasted. The only reading that teaches something is that the פסוק includes it in לבונה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? Said when a suggestion does not make sense
Granted, this part is fine
Well, it works out
Why do I need it? Meaning the פסוק would be unnecessary
We do not learn a one-time offering from offerings brought in all generations

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method of the גמרא: when a word could include or exclude, it picks the reading where the פסוק actually teaches something.

phrases.english: What is this?
Granted, if you say it comes to include, it works well.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לְהוֹצִיא – לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: But if you say it comes to exclude, why do I need it?
We do not learn a one-time offering from offerings of all generations.
phrases.notes: 'One-time' is the מנחת שמיני, brought only once. 'All generations' are the regular מנחות brought every year, like the עומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבּוֹת – שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the other reading would make the פסוק unnecessary.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe 'מנחה' excludes the מנחת שמיני from לבונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because שעה is not learned from דורות, an exclusion would be pointless, so the word includes the מנחת שמיני in לבונה.

steps.title: Why should 'היא' exclude the two loaves and not the priests' offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that the word 'היא' excludes the שתי הלחם from oil and לבונה. It then asks why the word should not exclude the מנחת כהנים instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'it is' comes to exclude the two loaves, so that they need neither oil nor frankincense. But maybe it excludes the priests' meal offering instead?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word in the ברייתא, 'היא', which excludes the שתי הלחם. It challenges this by suggesting the word might exclude the מנחת כהנים instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word is an exclusion, and the question is which offering it leaves out. Both the שתי הלחם and the מנחת כהנים are possible choices, so the גמרא asks why the ברייתא picked the שתי הלחם.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves brought on שבועות
Will require, will need
Oil mixed into or poured on a meal offering

phrases.english: "It is" – to exclude the two loaves,
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק: 'מנחה היא' (ויקרא 2:15).

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יִטְעֲנוּ לֹא שֶׁמֶן וְלֹא לְבוֹנָה.
phrases.english: so that they will require neither oil nor frankincense.
But say it excludes the priests' meal offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling 'מנחה', the גמרא moves to the next word of the ברייתא and asks the same kind of question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading that 'היא' excludes the שתי הלחם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exclusion could just as well apply to the מנחת כהנים, and nothing yet shows why the ברייתא chose the שתי הלחם.

steps.title: The priests' offering is more like the עומר in six ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it makes more sense to include the מנחת כהנים. Like the מנחת העומר, it is one עשרון, made holy in a כלי, is מצה, comes on its own, needs הגשה, and goes on the fire. The שתי הלחם differs in all six, so it is the one excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the priests' meal offering should be the one included, since it shares these features with the עומר: a tenth, a vessel, מצה, coming on its own, being brought near the altar, and the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by listing six ways the מנחת כהנים is like the מנחת העומר. So the מנחת כהנים stays included, and the שתי הלחם is the offering excluded by 'היא'. The very next line (אדרבה) challenges this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are one עשרון of flour, while the שתי הלחם is two. Both are made holy in a כלי, are מצה, come by themselves, are brought near the altar, and are burned on the fire. The שתי הלחם is חמץ, comes together with the lambs of שבועות, and is not burned on the altar. The more features an offering shares with the עומר, the more it belongs with it.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes more sense
A tenth of an איפה, a fixed measure of flour
A Temple service vessel that makes the offering holy
Unleavened, not chametz
Bringing the meal offering near to the corner of the altar
The fire on top of the altar

steps.whatToRemember: 'מנחה' includes the מנחת שמיני in לבונה, because excluding it would teach nothing. For 'היא', the גמרא first argues that the מנחת כהנים is like the עומר in six ways, so the שתי הלחם is the one excluded. The next step begins a challenge to this answer.

phrases.aramaic: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִנְחַת כֹּהֲנִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי,
phrases.english: It stands to reason that the priests' meal offering should be included,
since it is a tenth,
a vessel, matza, and itself,
phrases.notes: 'Itself' means it comes on its own, not together with another offering.

phrases.english: bringing near, and the fire.

steps.title: On the contrary: opening a counter-argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'אדרבה' to signal that it is about to argue the opposite of the answer it just gave.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. With the word 'אדרבה' it signals that it will now argue the reverse of what was just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27 the גמרא said the מנחת כהנים should be included because it shares six features with the מנחת העומר, so the שתי הלחם is the one left out. 'אדרבה' warns us that a reason is coming for the opposite view. The actual reason is not stated yet; it comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary: a signal that the גמרא is about to argue the reverse of the last statement
A flour offering brought by a כהן, which is fully burned

steps.confusionAlert: 'אדרבה' is not a final answer. It only opens a challenge, and the real argument comes in the next line.

phrases.english: On the contrary,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a counter-challenge to the answer in step 27, which included the מנחת כהנים because of its six shared features with the מנחת העומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion of step 27 that the מנחת כהנים is included and the שתי הלחם is excluded.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It signals that there may be a reason to see it the other way around. The reason itself comes in the next line.
